paragraphs: Ireland will need more hospital beds for people with serious mental illness. A new study says this.
The study is from the ESRI, a research group. It says Ireland may need up to 641 more beds by 2040. That is up to 37% more.
Why? There will be more people in Ireland, and more older people. In 2023, there were 1,015 short-stay beds for adults. There were 517 beds for long-term care.
Beds for teenagers may not go up. There will be fewer teenagers in 2040. But many young people wait a long time for help now.
Dr Aoife Brick wrote the study. She says more beds are not enough. People also need help near their homes. Minister Mary Butler says the study will help with planning.
sentZh: 愛爾蘭將需要更多病床給患有嚴重精神疾病的人。
一項新研究這麼說。
這項研究來自研究機構 ESRI。
研究說愛爾蘭到 2040 年可能需要多達 641 張額外病床。
也就是最多增加 37%。
為什麼？
愛爾蘭的人口會變多，老年人也會變多。
2023 年，成人短期住院病床有 1,015 張。
長期照護病床有 517 張。
青少年的病床可能不會增加。
2040 年青少年會變少。
但現在很多年輕人要等很久才能得到幫助。
伊法·布里克博士撰寫了這項研究。
她說只增加病床是不夠的。
人們也需要在住家附近得到協助。
部長瑪麗·巴特勒說這項研究將有助於規劃。

paragraphs: Ireland's mental health services will need up to 641 extra beds over the next 14 years, according to a new study from the Economic and Social Research Institute (ESRI).
The study says the number of beds in public psychiatric hospitals may need to rise by up to 37% by 2040. The main reasons are a growing population and more older people.

In 2023 there were 1,015 beds for adults who need short, intensive treatment. This number may need to grow by between 107 and 378. Beds for long-term care could rise from 517 to around 700. The Central Mental Hospital may also need up to 40 more beds.

The study does not expect more beds for children and teenagers, because there will be fewer people aged 13 to 17 in 2040. However, it warns that long waiting lists in local services make this hard to predict.

Dr Aoife Brick, who led the study, said the answer is not only more beds. People need the right mix of hospital care and help in their community. Mary Butler, the Minister of State for mental health, said the report will help the Government plan.
sentZh: 根據經濟與社會研究所（ESRI）的一項新研究，愛爾蘭的心理健康服務在未來 14 年將需要多達 641 張額外病床。
研究指出，到 2040 年公立精神科醫院的病床數可能需要增加多達 37%。
主要原因是人口成長和老年人增加。
2023 年，供需要短期密集治療的成人使用的病床有 1,015 張。
這個數字可能需要增加 107 到 378 張。
長期照護病床可能從 517 張增加到約 700 張。
中央精神病院也可能需要最多 40 張額外病床。
研究預計兒童和青少年的病床不會增加，因為 2040 年 13 至 17 歲的人口會減少。
不過研究也警告，地方服務的候診名單很長，使這一點難以預測。
主持研究的伊法·布里克博士說，解決辦法不只是增加病床。
人們需要醫院照護與社區協助的適當搭配。
心理健康國務部長瑪麗·巴特勒說，這份報告將幫助政府做規劃。

paragraphs: Ireland's mental health system will require as many as 641 additional beds over the next 14 years to keep up with rising demand, according to a study by the Economic and Social Research Institute (ESRI).

The research, funded by the Department of Health, projects that capacity in public psychiatric inpatient services may need to increase by up to 37% by 2040, driven mainly by population growth and ageing.

In 2023, the public system had 1,015 acute adult beds for short-term, intensive treatment, a figure that may need to rise by between 107 and 378. Continuing-care beds for people with severe and enduring illness could grow from 517 to about 710, while the Central Mental Hospital may need between 16 and 40 more.

No increase is forecast for child and adolescent inpatient beds, as the teenage population is expected to fall. Even so, the ESRI cautions that long waiting lists in community services make future demand uncertain.

Lead author Dr Aoife Brick stressed that the solution is not simply more beds but the right balance of inpatient and community care. Minister of State Mary Butler said the findings would guide planning as services expand.
sentZh: 根據經濟與社會研究所（ESRI）的研究，愛爾蘭的心理健康體系在未來 14 年將需要多達 641 張額外病床，才能跟上日益增加的需求。
這項由衛生部資助的研究預測，到 2040 年公立精神科住院服務的容量可能需要增加多達 37%，主要受人口成長與高齡化推動。
2023 年，公立體系有 1,015 張供短期密集治療的成人急性病床，這個數字可能需要增加 107 到 378 張。
供嚴重且長期患病者使用的持續照護病床可能從 517 張增加到約 710 張，而中央精神病院可能需要再增加 16 到 40 張。
由於青少年人口預計會減少，兒童及青少年住院病床預測不會增加。
即便如此，ESRI 提醒，社區服務的候診名單很長，使未來需求充滿不確定性。
主要作者伊法·布里克博士強調，解決之道不只是增加病床，而是住院與社區照護之間的適當平衡。
國務部長瑪麗·巴特勒說，這些研究結果將在服務擴展時指引規劃。

paragraphs: Ireland's mental health services will need up to 641 additional beds within 14 years if they are to keep pace with mounting demand, a study by the Economic and Social Research Institute (ESRI) has concluded.

The research, funded by the Department of Health, forecasts that public psychiatric inpatient capacity may have to expand by as much as 37% by 2040, a trend fuelled chiefly by a burgeoning and ageing population.

The public system had 1,015 acute adult beds in 2023, earmarked for short but intensive episodes of care, and this tally may need to swell by between 107 and 378. Continuing-care provision for those with severe, enduring illness could climb from 517 beds to roughly 710, while the Central Mental Hospital may require up to 40 more.

Paediatric inpatient numbers are not projected to rise, given an anticipated contraction in the teenage population. The ESRI nonetheless warns that protracted waiting lists in community services render any such forecast precarious.

Lead author Dr Aoife Brick emphasised that beds alone are no panacea; what matters is an appropriate blend of inpatient and community provision. Minister of State Mary Butler said the findings would inform planning as services are scaled up.
sentZh: 經濟與社會研究所（ESRI）的一項研究得出結論：愛爾蘭的心理健康服務若要跟上不斷攀升的需求，14 年內將需要多達 641 張額外病床。
這項由衛生部資助的研究預測，到 2040 年公立精神科住院容量可能必須擴充多達 37%，這一趨勢主要由迅速增長且日益老化的人口所推動。
2023 年公立體系有 1,015 張成人急性病床，專供短期但密集的治療，而這個總數可能需要增加 107 到 378 張。
為嚴重且長期患病者提供的持續照護可能從 517 張病床攀升至約 710 張，而中央精神病院可能需要最多再增加 40 張。
由於預期青少年人口將會縮減，兒科住院病床數預計不會上升。
不過 ESRI 警告，社區服務冗長的候診名單使任何此類預測都很不穩固。
主要作者伊法·布里克博士強調，光靠病床並非萬靈丹；重要的是住院與社區服務的適當結合。
國務部長瑪麗·巴特勒說，在服務擴大之際，這些研究結果將為規劃提供依據。

paragraphs: According to a study conducted by the Economic and Social Research Institute (ESRI), Ireland's mental health services will require up to 641 additional beds over the next 14 years in order to accommodate increasing demand.

The research, which was commissioned and funded by the Department of Health, projects that public psychiatric inpatient capacity may need to rise by as much as 37% by 2040. This increase is attributable primarily to population growth and demographic ageing.

In 2023, the public system comprised 1,015 acute adult beds, a figure which may need to increase by between 107 and 378. Similarly, continuing-care beds for individuals with severe and enduring illness are projected to rise from 517 to approximately 710, while the Central Mental Hospital may require up to 40 further beds.

By contrast, no growth is anticipated in child and adolescent inpatient provision, owing to a projected decline in the teenage population. Nevertheless, the ESRI notes that substantial waiting lists in community services render future demand inherently uncertain.

The lead author, Dr Aoife Brick, emphasised that an effective response is contingent upon an appropriate balance between inpatient and community care, rather than bed numbers alone. Mary Butler, Minister of State for mental health, stated that the findings would inform future planning.
sentZh: 根據經濟與社會研究所（ESRI）進行的一項研究，愛爾蘭的心理健康服務在未來 14 年將需要多達 641 張額外病床，以因應日益增加的需求。
這項由衛生部委託並資助的研究預測，到 2040 年公立精神科住院容量可能需要增加多達 37%。
此一增加主要可歸因於人口成長與人口結構高齡化。
2023 年，公立體系共有 1,015 張成人急性病床，這個數字可能需要增加 107 到 378 張。
同樣地，供嚴重且長期患病者使用的持續照護病床預計將從 517 張增加到約 710 張，而中央精神病院可能需要最多再增加 40 張病床。
相較之下，由於預計青少年人口下降，兒童及青少年住院服務預期不會成長。
然而 ESRI 指出，社區服務大量的候診名單使未來需求本質上就充滿不確定性。
主要作者伊法·布里克博士強調，有效的因應取決於住院與社區照護之間的適當平衡，而非僅僅取決於病床數量。
心理健康國務部長瑪麗·巴特勒表示，這些研究結果將為未來的規劃提供依據。

paragraphs: Ireland's mental health system will require as many as 641 additional beds over the next 14 years to keep up with rising demand, according to a study by the Economic and Social Research Institute (ESRI).

The research, funded by the Department of Health, projects that capacity in public psychiatric inpatient services may need to increase by up to 37% by 2040, driven mainly by population growth and ageing.

In 2023, the public system had 1,015 acute adult beds for short-term, intensive treatment, a figure that may need to rise by between 107 and 378. Continuing-care beds for people with severe and enduring illness could grow from 517 to about 710, while the Central Mental Hospital may need between 16 and 40 more.

No increase is forecast for child and adolescent inpatient beds, as the teenage population is expected to fall. Even so, the ESRI cautions that long waiting lists in community services make future demand uncertain.

Lead author Dr Aoife Brick stressed that the solution is not simply more beds but the right balance of inpatient and community care. Minister of State Mary Butler said the findings would guide planning as services expand.
